{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** Legal (Customer-side review)
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — 18 rules assessed

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against 18 playbook rules. Ten clauses are compliant and require no redline; eight are deviations, of which two are critical (indemnification and limitation of liability) and three more sit in walk-away territory (exclusivity, licence scope and non-compete).

The core problem is a cluster of one-sided commercial restraints and risk allocations: Vendor takes a one-way indemnity from us with no Vendor indemnity anywhere in the Agreement; both Parties are capped at one month of Fees "without exception", which overrides the Excluded Claims regime in §§ 21.2–21.3; we are locked into a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment, sole-source exclusivity for the full term, and a 24-month, unlimited-territory post-term non-compete; the Services licence is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion and excludes Affiliates and contractors; and § 11.1 requires immediate cessation of assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data with no export.

Several of these restraints contradict § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. That internal conflict supports our position and should be used in negotiation.

The news is better elsewhere. Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data (§§ 13.2, 14.1–14.4), assignment and change of control (§ 24), termination for convenience (§ 9.4), auto-renewal mechanics and the CPI/3% uplift cap (§§ 8.2–8.3), audit rights (§ 22), governing law and venue (§ 28), insurance (§ 18), and the absence of any liquidated damages, MFN or non-solicit burden on us all sit at or above our preferred position.

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 20.1 (and dangling cross-reference in § 9.3) | One-way Customer indemnity for "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services"; no Vendor indemnity anywhere. We added a Vendor defence/indemnity (IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice, control of defence and cooperation, and narrowed our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our breach of Applicable Law. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | §§ 21.1–21.3 ("Fees" defined at § 1.5) | Mutual cap of one month of Fees actually paid, applying "without exception" and so overriding Excluded Claims. Below the 12-month fallback and below the 6-month floor. We set the cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, restored the Excluded Claims carve-outs, and conformed § 21.3 to reach our payment obligations generally. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 2.2 (conflicts with § 12.3) | Vendor as sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics for the full three-year term, with no category limit, no 12-month cap and no performance-based exit. We made Vendor non-exclusive, which also resolves the conflict with § 12.3. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 13.1 (cf. §§ 13.2–13.3) | Services licence is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion and expressly excludes Affiliates and contractors. We extended it to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf and limited revocation to uncured material breach, aligning with § 13.3. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (conflicts with § 12.3) | 24-month post-term non-compete, undefined scope, unlimited territory, no internal-development or acquisition carve-out. We converted the prohibition into an express permission, leaving the balance of the sentence intact. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 (conflicts with §§ 7.1, 9.4, 12.3) | Three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights". We removed the commitment and confirmed we pay only for Services used or ordered. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Deviation | § 11.1 (conflicts with §§ 11.2–11.3) | Immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data, with no export or migration support. We substituted up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates and anchored the § 11.2 30-day return to expiry or termination. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 19.2 (remedies at § 19.4) | Deliverable/software conformance warranty limited to fifteen days, with no correction or refund obligation thereafter — below the 90-day fallback floor. We extended it to ninety days and confirmed it reaches software delivered to us; § 19.4 remedies preserved. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | §§ 13.2, 14.1–14.4 (with § 1.8, § 15.1) | Preferred position: present assignment of Deliverables to us, Vendor retained rights limited to Vendor Technology, perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free licence to us and Affiliates, Customer Data processing limited to service delivery, no joint ownership absent a signed instrument. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | §§ 24.1–24.4 (with § 13.3) | Free Customer assignment to Affiliates and successors; Vendor assignment and change-of-control transfer require our consent; no Vendor exit or repricing on our change of control. Competitor bar is framed as consent-based rather than absolute — noted only. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 9.4 (also §§ 7.1, 22.2, 27.3) | No liquidated damages, penalty, termination fee or minimum-fee charge payable by us; convenience termination is fee-limited with refund of prepaid Fees. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9.4 | Preferred position: 30 days' notice, pro rata refund, no early-termination fee, and no corresponding Vendor convenience right during a committed term. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | §§ 22.1–22.3 | Once per twelve months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor bears costs absent a 5% underpayment, no direct system access. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | §§ 28.1–28.3 | New York law, exclusive jurisdiction in New York County state and federal courts, no arbitration; pre-suit escalation does not displace the forum or delay urgent relief. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 12.3 (with §§ 7.1, 8.3) | No MFN, benchmarking or right-to-match mechanic; § 12.3 expressly confirms no most-favoured-customer commitment. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 (cf. § 30.1) | No non-solicit or no-hire covenant; § 12.3 confirms we may hire any person responding to general recruitment. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | §§ 8.2–8.3 | Twelve-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension if missed, uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §§ 18.1–18.2 | CGL USD 1M/2M, workers' compensation, E&O USD 2M, cyber and privacy USD 5M, certificates on request, primary coverage, no limitation of liability. |

## 3. Walk-away items

The following provisions sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and must be resolved before signature:

1. **§ 20.1 — absent Vendor indemnity.** A one-way indemnity from us covering "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services", with no Vendor indemnity for third-party IP infringement or misconduct anywhere in the Agreement.
2. **§ 21.1 — one-month liability cap applying "without exception".** Below the 6-month floor and it collapses the Excluded Claims regime in §§ 21.2–21.3, so indemnities, confidentiality, data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement all sit inside a one-month cap. The § 1.5 definition of "Fees" narrows the base further by excluding taxes, expenses and implementation charges.
3. **§ 2.2 — full-term sole-source exclusivity** with no category limit, no 12-month cap and no exit for service-level or delivery failure.
4. **§ 13.1 — Services licence revocable at Vendor's sole discretion** and excluding Affiliates and contractors, with "Customer" defined as a single entity.
5. **§ 12.4 — 24-month post-term non-compete** of undefined scope and unlimited territory, with no carve-outs.
6. **§ 2.1 — three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay** expressly "without reduction or termination rights".
7. **§ 11.1 — immediate cessation of assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data** with no export or migration support.

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the eight deviations, leading with §§ 20.1 and 21.1 as the two critical items and presenting the five remaining walk-away provisions as a package.
2. **Use the internal conflicts as leverage.** Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4 each contradict § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer or minimum-volume commitment; § 11.1 contradicts §§ 11.2–11.3; and § 13.1's "non-transferable" wording contradicts § 13.3. The § 2.2 precedence provision resolves only Order Form and exhibit conflicts, so these must be fixed on the face of the document.
3. **On liability**, hold the mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, restore the Excluded Claims carve-outs and conform § 21.3. Note the drafting choice on indemnities: because § 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims, we did not volunteer the fallback 3x-annual-fees super-cap; keep that in reserve only if a super-cap becomes the price of agreement.
4. **Housekeeping to raise in the next turn:** conform the § 9.3 cross-reference to the non-existent § 20.5 of infringement remedies.
5. **Two redlines were repaired on verification** (§ 21.1 limitation of liability and § 19.2 warranty duration) — confirm the final language reads through cleanly against §§ 21.2–21.3 and § 19.4 before the draft goes out.
6. **Positions noted but not pursued**, available as trade material if Vendor pushes back elsewhere: the § 24.2 competitor bar framed as consent-based rather than absolute; "subject to payment of the applicable Fees" in the ownership grant and the § 14.4 opt-in to joint ownership; the 12-month software warranty period and § 19.3's limitation of malicious-code cover to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor"."}
